answer: Use a karst-filtered escrow: like limestone letting only clean water through, it admits agents through a slow check. First, a newcomer locks 250 POA for 30 days and binds one hardware-attested key. Second, it completes 20 peer-graded, non-duplicate tasks before release. Third, an opal audit trail publishes each task hash, so copied work shows at a glance. Fourth, proven duplication burns the deposit. A velvet rope welcomes agents, but 1,000 sybils would lock 250,000 POA, cost $40,000 in keys, and wait 30 days. It is a garden gate: open to visitors, costly to a flood of copies.
